# Apex Flow Web Scraper

> Web scraper that turns any web page, PDF or DOCX into clean Markdown. Self-hosted, no API key, no per-page fee. Built by Apex Flow Labs. Version 0.2.0 (5 November 2026).

## What it does
- Converts pages to Markdown with headings, GFM tables, fenced code with language, absolute links; removes navigation, cookie banners and hidden elements.
- Renders JavaScript pages in an isolated Brave browser, with screenshots on request.
- Reads PDF, DOCX, RSS/Atom feeds and JSON.
- Maps sites (robots.txt, nested and gzip sitemaps), crawls with durable jobs, change tracking with diffs.
- Owned full-text search (SQLite FTS5, BM25) over everything scraped.
- JSON-Schema extraction using DeepSeek first, OpenRouter second.
- MCP tools for agents: fetch, map, crawl, search, compare.
- Obeys robots.txt and Crawl-delay; fetches public addresses only.

## Measured results (30 public URLs, 94 hand-checked reference checks, 5 Nov 2026)
- 26 of 30 URLs fetched; 92 of 94 Markdown fidelity checks passed (97.9%).
- Median 1,454 ms per URL; median process memory 56.4 MB.
- Versus Firecrawl (free keyless tier, same checks, hand-scored) on 24 URLs with references: 91/93 vs 85/93; we score higher on 6 pages, tie on 18, lower on 0. Firecrawl returned content for all 30 URLs; we returned 26 (two blocked by robots.txt that we obey, two by bot walls).

## Not claimed
- No CAPTCHA solving or bot-wall evasion; zillow.com and glassdoor.com block it.
- Search covers sites you have indexed, not the whole web.
- The hosted API, accounts and billing are planned and not live. Planned pricing: Free 1,000 pages; $19 for 25,000; $79 for 150,000; $299 for 750,000.

## Usage
Python: `from rainbo_scrape import scrape; scrape("https://example.com").markdown`
CLI: `rainbo-scrape fetch https://example.com`
